What is Azeroth Survivors?

Last updated: October 29, 2026

Field guide

What is Azeroth Survivors?How to playBuildsTier listDownload & fixesSafety checkTalent treeLuck

Azeroth Survivors is a free, fan-made browser roguelike created by Aethus. It uses World of Warcraft's classes, zones and spell names, but it is not a Blizzard product and not connected to the WoW client. You open it in a WebGPU-capable browser, pick a race and a class, and survive a roughly 16-minute zone run where your abilities cast themselves and your only inputs are movement and level-up card choices.

Quick facts

FactDetails
DeveloperAethus
PriceFree

Account requiredNo
Run length~16 min
Classes9

What it is not

It is not a private server, not a WoW addon, and not a download-and-install MMO. The whole run happens locally in your browser; there is no account system and no persistent online character. Two CurseForge addons with similar names run inside WoW Forever and are different games — do not confuse them with this browser roguelike.

The core loop

The loop is survivors-like: enemies spawn in waves, your spells fire automatically, and every level-up deals three cards — a new spell, a rank-up, or a passive. Cards are color-coded by estimated damage, but color is a hint, not a guarantee. You can reroll the hand with R. Between runs, you keep boss gear, collection progress and a 51-point talent tree that can be reset.

What you need

The real requirement is WebGPU. Chrome and Edge are the safe starting point; Safari works on 26 and above. It is a keyboard-and-mouse game — mobile is not a supported target. First load pulls the whole world into the browser, so a slow first load is expected; repeated reloading makes it worse.
